title: Dispatch: Fix campaign-rule lifecycle admission (PR #524 blocking review, attempt 4)
description:
Dispatch of eshyra-jhpt.2 (attempt 4) — blocking review defect on PR #524.

PR #524 (head 2d6b7c7) received a BLOCKING review under the semantic-system profile (GitHub review #5097504606): campaign-rule lifecycle admission can rewrite canonical history. The supervisor independently reproduced all four sub-claims before dispatching this; the probe output is quoted below so you can write tests that fail today.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.2.4 on branch eshyra-jhpt.2.4, cut from the integration branch eshyra-jhpt (2d6b7c7, the exact reviewed head). Work only inside that worktree.
*** Run `npm ci` in this worktree FIRST, before any verification *** — a fresh worktree has no node_modules and packages/cli tests will otherwise resolve @eshyra/core up to the parent checkout on main and report a false green (tracked as eshyra-3dmq). The supervisor has already run npm ci here, but re-run it if anything looks off, and confirm node_modules/@eshyra/core resolves INTO this worktree before trusting a result.

ROOT CAUSE
revokeCampaignRule guards `if (existing.status !== 'active') throw`, but supersedeCampaignRule has no equivalent guard on the prior rule's status. Worse, it then calls validateCampaignRules with `{ ...prior, status: 'superseded', supersededBy: input.successor.ruleIdentity }` — it OVERWRITES the prior's real status before validating, so validation structurally cannot observe that the rule was already superseded or revoked. The create path (writeRule) has matching admission holes.

REPRODUCED (supervisor probe against 2d6b7c7, all four passing i.e. all four defects present):

CLAIM 1 — re-superseding a superseded rule overwrites its original successor and corrupts history:
    old.supersededBy after second supersede: second (was "first")
    active at position 7: [ 'old', 'first' ]   <- old overlaps its own first successor
  This is the severe one. After `old` is superseded by `first` (effective 5) and then again by `second` (effective 9), the historical active-at-position query at 7 returns BOTH `old` and `first` as active, because the stored supersededBy now points at `second` and the "successor.effective_position > cutoff" predicate no longer excludes `old`. eshyra-jhpt.4 auditor parity and eshyra-jhpt.8 replay both read that query.

CLAIM 2 — a revoked rule can be converted to superseded, keeping its revocation position:
    revoked rule status after supersede: superseded | supersededBy: s
  The revocation is silently erased from the rule's status while revoked_position remains set.

CLAIM 3 — createCampaignRule accepts a revoked rule whose revocation precedes its own effective position:
    created revoked-before-effective rule: bad  (effective ordinal 10, revoked at 2)
  revokeCampaignRule enforces this ordering; the direct create path does not.

CLAIM 4 — createCampaignRule accepts a superseded rule with a dangling successor reference:
    created superseded rule pointing at: does-not-exist  (no such rule)
  validateCampaignRule (singular) checks only that supersededBy is non-null for a superseded rule; the referential check lives in validateCampaignRules (plural), which the create path never calls.

REQUIRED FIX
1. supersedeCampaignRule must reject a prior rule that is not `active`, with CampaignRuleError, BEFORE any mutation — mirroring revokeCampaignRule's existing guard. Distinct messages for already-superseded and revoked are preferable.
2. Do not let validation be fed a rewritten status. Validate the prior rule's ACTUAL admission state first; keep the existing validateCampaignRules pair call for the post-transition shape, but it must no longer be the only thing standing between a bad transition and the database.
3. writeRule / createCampaignRule must enforce, for a directly created rule: a revoked rule requires revokedPosition >= effectivePosition (reuse compareCampaignPositions, matching revokeCampaignRule); and a superseded rule's supersededBy must reference an existing rule in the same campaign, rejecting a dangling reference. Decide deliberately whether directly creating an already-superseded or already-revoked rule should be permitted at all, and say why in your notes — if you keep it, it must be fully validated; if you forbid it, the checkpoint/restore path must still be able to reconstruct historical rows, so verify the restore tests still pass and explain how history is rehydrated.
4. Cross-check the rest of the lifecycle surface for the same admission class while you are here: any other transition that mutates status or a lifecycle position without first checking the current state. Report what you found, including "nothing further" if that is the answer.

REQUIRED PERMANENT REGRESSION COVERAGE (the review names these explicitly)
  a. Re-superseding an already-superseded rule is rejected, AND an active-at-position assertion proves the original supersession chain is intact (the position-7 case above must show exactly one of old/first active, never both).
  b. Superseding a revoked rule is rejected, and the rule remains revoked with its revocation position unchanged.
  c. Direct creation of a revoked rule with revokedPosition < effectivePosition is rejected.
  d. Direct creation of a superseded rule with a dangling supersededBy is rejected.
  e. Whatever you decide for point 3's "permitted at all" question, cover the decision.
These must be real regression tests that fail against 2d6b7c7 — verify that by checking out the old campaignRuleStore.ts into your worktree, confirming the new tests fail, then restoring your fix. Report the failure count you observed.

SCOPE
Storage admission and validation only. Do not change the active-at-position predicate itself, the projection, the seam contract, the migrations, the position encoding, or anything in .3. No new features.

VERIFICATION
`npm ci` first, then `npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing (it rewrites files). In your notes state the pass/skip counts and confirm @eshyra/core resolved into this worktree.
